After almost 20 years, this game still leaves many modern games in a shame with its detailed graphics, level design and sound engineering.

A definitive improvement over the original PC port since the latest patch (Dec 20th).

The reasons to pick this one up over the original:

- 60 fps physics.
- Adjustable FOV with weapon viewmodels adjusted to look good on PC (no more giant weapon models that take up half your screen).
- Better mouse controls.
- The survivor difficulty from the PS3 release is in the remastered version and it's the best way to play the game if you want a challenge.
- Higher resolution textures on most assets (including the weapon models which is a really nice plus compared to the low resolution models of the original game).
- Significantly improved rendering (newer DirectX basically)
- No compatibility issues (the original game can have all sorts of weird compatibility bugs on newer systems).
What a beautiful and charming experience... sort of the kind of game you should be playing during the Christmas season.

Haiku, the Robot is so very close to being good, but a lack of original ideas makes this one the rare miss for me in the Metroidvania genre.  I know it is easy to be an armchair developer and say "Well you should have just made the game good instead!" but so often during my playthrough I felt like I was just going through the motions even when I was actively trying to be engaged.  Its not just that it is easy, even though it is, its more so that none of the systems OR ideas clicked with me in any meaningful way.  This is a shame because clearly a lot of polish went into making the game look and feel good, but that just isnt enough sometimes.

The first time I tried this title was quite a while ago on PlayStation 3. I was much younger and never actually finished it, not because I didn't like it, but because I kept stretching out my playthrough until I eventually forgot about it. However, after a long time, I decided to play it again, but now on PC, and holy cow, I didn’t remember the game being this good. The story, the gameplay, the mechanics, the graphics, the performance, the atmosphere, everything in this game is incredibly polished. So polished, in fact, that I finished it in just two sessions. Honestly, I think it's an amazing game, and if you're looking for a demanding action title that’s a bit different from the rest, this one is perfect.

Once cleared continue to enemy filled zone, kill them (still pressing Q in every hallway so you don't miss any of the hundreds of similar collectibles), get to new base camp. Rinse and repeat for about 15 hours.

The lack of combat in Animal Well lends itself well to the game world that begs to be explored. The puzzles are intuitive and are the collectibles are cleverly hidden. Once you finish the main quest and have collected all the collectables the game begins to diverge from being a puzzle game and leans into being more of an ARG. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, but something to be aware of if you want to see everything this game has to offer.

One thing to note if you're going to play on Steam Deck is the battery life with the default settings is a bit lacklustre, but that is easily fixed by changing these settings in the performance tab.
Refresh Rate: 60Hz
TDP Limit: 5 Watts
Manual GPU Clock: 800 MHz

I bought this game because I love Shogun Showdown and this seemed like the same type of game except action/real-time instead of turn based with a feature called Forestrike to basically let you practice because fights need to be executed perfectly. Then, it went into my backlog, but added to my favorites because I really enjoyed the few minutes of what I tried and meant to get back to it. Well I finally picked it up to give it a proper go and it is indeed really good, fun, and actually has a good story that doesn't seem too intrusive in the gameplay. There are a lot of moves and features in here giving you multiple ways you can play and try to execute your fights which is very cool. I still have tons to discover but this is definitely a quality game that's worth the price, especially if you like Shogun Showdown and basically want that except not turn-based.

Reanimal is the kind of horror game that sticks with you long after you close it. The atmosphere is insanely dark and disturbing, every area feels handcrafted with creepy detail, and the sound design constantly keeps you on edge. It perfectly captures that unsettling feeling of being trapped in a nightmare you can’t wake up from.

The creature designs are absolutely terrifying, and the co-op aspect makes every moment even more intense. One second you’re exploring in silence, the next you’re both panicking trying to survive whatever nightmare just crawled out of the shadows.

You can really feel the influence from the creators of Little Nightmares, but Reanimal takes the horror to a whole new level. If you love cinematic horror games with amazing visuals, tension, and unforgettable monsters, this is easily one to watch.
